plan: Since this functions as a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid, equivalent to the clock stopping at the second-highest exit price), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $48 to maximize expected profit.

This is structurally similar to a second-price auction since the sealed bid acts as an exit price, and the winner pays the clock price when the second-to-last bidder exits (i.e., the second-highest bid). In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding below value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above risks winning at a loss. I will bid exactly my true value of $38.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the ascending clock ends when the second-highest bidder exits, and the winner pays that price), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly $12 ensures I win whenever the highest competing bid is below $12, paying only that competing bid, and I avoid overpaying if others bid higher. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down in this mechanism.
